features.note: The enclosure reads clearly as a walled heat boundary. The exhaust-wall preset pair is the decisive evidence: coupling-exhaust-off.png shows a solid dark panel (blades flat, aperture closed); coupling-exhaust-full.png shows the same panel as an open grille with the two exhaust fan hubs visible through the blade gaps. The state change is unambiguous at a glance — fully qualifies as a boundary heat does or does not cross. compressor-room.png establishes an opaque solid room from inside the bay; compressor-room-open.png reveals interior contents on toggle, confirming containment. The enclosure is properly distinct from loose equipment.

luminaire-grid.png is a near-featureless grey plane — almost certainly a near-perpendicular overhead or straight-up shot that compresses 0.35 m discs at 7 m height to invisible specks. No 6×3 grid is countable; no individual fixture reads as a finned disc or lit lens; the camera preset fails its evidencing role entirely. Fixtures are present in duct-run.png and the hero views as small hanging pendants, confirming they exist, but their form, count, and regularity cannot be verified from any available capture. Below threshold.

Air path is continuous and unbroken. ahu-roof.png shows the AHU box sitting above the roof slab with a metallic riser cylinder descending into the bay and transitioning into the trunk duct — the joint reads as embedded with no gap. duct-run.png shows the trunk duct running the full bay length with green flow-direction indicators along the underside. The riser-to-duct connection is unambiguous. No floating segments. Diffusers are represented as green flow cones on the duct underside, acceptable at blockout. The air path reads coherently from unit to space.

compressor-room-open.png reveals two featureless dark cuboids (lead and lag compressors), a blue vertical cylinder (receiver — correctly shaped and colored for an ASME vessel), and a smaller dark box (dryer). The spatial arrangement is plausible for the ref layout. However, neither compressor box carries any cooling-fan grille, top-fan disc, or canopy surface break that would identify them as rotary screw packages rather than storage crates. The air header pipe is a barely-visible thin white line. The receiver is the only component with a distinct identity. The skid as a unit does not read as described. Below threshold.

The bay reads as a real industrial structure. Wall cladding panels are visible with column posts at regular intervals consistent with 8 m spacing. The 2:1 plan ratio (40×20 m) is geometrically correct. bay-envelope.png with roof ON shows a fully closed building convincingly, with the AHU visible on the roof. The flat profile (5:1 length-to-height) is the correct geometry for a 40×8 m section and is not a framing defect. Roof truss elements are not visible in the open-roof default view — this is the sole weakness. The bay does not read as a hollow box; the internal systems (duct, luminaires, enclosure bump) add readable depth.

important_features.note: The air_header_piping from compressor to receiver is a barely-visible thin white wire in compressor-room-open.png. The distribution_main (~29 m run at high level along the bay) is not clearly readable as an intentional element in any capture; it may be present as a thin line along the wall in duct-run.png but cannot be confirmed with confidence. The routing does not visibly cut through structure, which is correct, but the pipe's presence is not established.

The gold human figure is clearly readable in duct-run.png at the center of the bay floor — it makes the 8 m clear height and the trunk duct elevation legible at a glance. The figure is not visible in the hero view (index.png), likely occluded by the compressor enclosure from the 42°/24° camera. The feature functions where it appears; it just misses the primary frame.

defects.description: The luminaire-grid camera preset produces a near-uniform grey plane. The 18-fixture 6×3 grid is uncountable; no individual disc form, no finned housing, and no lit lens is visible. The dedicated evidencing capture is non-functional. The spec threshold (0.75) cannot be met without a capture that actually shows the array.

The lead and lag compressor packages are featureless dark cuboids with no cooling-fan grille, no top-fan disc, and no canopy surface variation. They cannot be identified as rotary screw machines by visual inspection. The air header piping is a barely-visible thin line. Only the receiver cylinder has recognisable identity.

Roof trusses are absent from the open-roof default view. The spec requires the bay to read as a structure with roof trusses. The wall-top edge is a plain flat line at 8 m with no truss chords or structure visible above it.

The distribution_main (receiver to bay end, ~29 m at approx. 5.5 m height along the wall) is not clearly readable as an intentional element. The pipe is either absent from the camera's visible region or too thin to distinguish from the wall structure.

The scale reference figure is not visible in the hero view. Current pivot [4.0, 0.0, 2.0] places the figure likely occluded behind the compressor enclosure from the 42°/24° hero camera. The figure exists and functions in duct-run.png but is absent from the primary frame.

corrections.instruction: Reposition the luminaire-grid camera to azimuth ~200°, elevation ~-35° (oblique upward from inside the bay, looking at the ceiling array from below at an angle) so the 6×3 grid of discs is seen in perspective with enough angular separation to read individual fixtures. Set dim=65 for this camera preset so the emissive lenses glow and the grid is immediately countable. A straight-up or straight-down shot at any angle renders 0.35 m discs at 7 m as invisible specks — use oblique perspective.

Add a flattened cylinder (radius 0.28 m, height 0.10 m) centred on the top face of each compressor box to represent the cooling-fan housing. Subdivide the disc surface with 6 radial blade slots (or apply a darker annular ring) to read as a fan grille. No full fan model is needed — a disc with surface variation is sufficient to distinguish each box as a machine at blockout. Also increase the air_header_piping geometry radius to at least 0.05 m so the connection from compressor to receiver is visible as a pipe, not a wire.

Move roof_trusses out of the roof layer group so they remain visible when the roof cladding layer is toggled off. At blockout, trusses can be flat horizontal bars or extruded I-section profiles running bay-width (20 m) at 8 m, spaced at the 8 m column pitch. They must be readable in the default open-roof hero view — they are structure, not cladding.

Ensure the distribution_main mesh uses a tube radius of 0.04 m (half of spec header_pipe_diameter_m 0.08) and is routed visibly from the receiver outlet (+15.5, 2.36, −7.5) along the bay wall to the far end, running at approximately 5.5 m height. Add at least four pipe-hanger supports along the run (simple thin vertical rods from the wall) to read as an intentionally routed element rather than a stray line.

Move the scale_reference_figure pivot to approximately [4.0, 0.0, 6.0] so it stands clear of the compressor enclosure footprint and is visible in the 42°/24° hero camera. Verify visibility by checking that the figure's bounding box does not overlap the enclosure mesh in the hero view's projection.

mechanical.note: All budgets are nominal. 69 draws and 7332 tris leave substantial headroom for later passes. 34/34 tests cover simulation invariants and dashboard model contracts.
